title: High-Speed Propane & Electric Floor Burnishing Pricing: Small Suites vs. Large Floors
seoTitle: Small vs Large Office Floor Burnishing Pricing: Volume & Scale Rates
metaDescription: Small vs large office floor burnishing: effective rates fall from about $0.05–$0.07 per sq ft at 2,000 sq ft to $0.012–$0.025 at 60,000. Compare bids free.
excerpt: The same burnishing visit can cost five times more per square foot in a 2,000 sq ft suite than on a 60,000 sq ft floor plate. Here is how minimums, machine choice and route density create that gap, and what small tenants can do to buy like a large one.
quickAnswer: Small suites of about 2,000 sq ft usually pay the $90–$135 per-visit minimum, which works out to roughly $0.045–$0.068 per sq ft of hard floor. Mid-size offices of 6,000–15,000 sq ft fall to about $0.02–$0.05, and buildings with 25,000+ sq ft of hard floor that allow propane machines can reach $0.012–$0.025 per sq ft per pass. The breakpoints are the minimum charge at the low end and the switch from electric to propane at the high end.

blocks.text: Why Scale Changes Burnishing Unit Prices So Sharply

Burnishing has a high fixed cost and a very low variable cost. Unloading a machine, checking the pad, dust mopping, setting cones and loading back out takes 20–40 minutes whether the floor is 1,500 sq ft or 15,000 sq ft. The actual burnish pass on open floor runs 6,000–9,000 sq ft per hour with a 20-inch electric unit and 12,000–20,000 sq ft per hour with a 27-inch propane unit. Spread fixed time over a small floor and it dominates the bill; spread it over a large floor and it nearly disappears.

The same curve shows up in general janitorial pricing. National base rates run $0.12–$0.20 per sq ft per visit for offices under 2,500 sq ft and $0.05–$0.10 for buildings above 25,000 sq ft. Burnishing follows that slope even more steeply because the task is so fast once the machine is rolling.

blocks.caption: Effective high-speed burnishing cost per visit by hard-floor area (national ranges, route add-on pricing)

blocks.text: Notice the jump between 2,000 and 6,000 sq ft: the per-visit cost doubles or triples while the area triples, so the effective rate drops by a third. Between 15,000 and 30,000 sq ft, the change in machine type does most of the work. Above 60,000 sq ft, savings flatten because the vendor needs a second operator and a second machine to fit the shift window.
Small Suites: Living With the Minimum

In a 2,000 sq ft medical, legal or insurance suite, often only half the floor is hard surface: reception, a breakroom, a hallway and a restroom approach. At $0.04 per sq ft, 1,000 sq ft of VCT should cost $40, yet the vendor will bill the $90–$135 minimum. Small tenants have three ways to stop overpaying.

items: Bundle the burnish into the nightly visit the janitorial crew already makes, so the minimum is absorbed by the base contract rather than charged as a separate trip.
Lengthen the interval in low-traffic suites from weekly to biweekly or monthly, so each minimum charge buys a visible gloss improvement rather than maintenance on an already shiny floor.
Coordinate with neighboring suites or the landlord so one crew burnishes the common corridor and several suites in a single mobilization, splitting the minimum.
Ask whether a battery burnisher is on the route truck; cordless units save 10–15 minutes of cord management in cramped suites.

blocks.title: Small-suite finish care
blocks.text: In small spaces, gloss problems usually trace to the floor finish, not the burnisher. When the vendor lays fresh coats during a recoat, a dedicated finish applicator such as the Rubbermaid Commercial flat mop kit with its 18-inch pad produces thin, streak-free coats that burnish to a hard shine instead of smearing.
Large Floors: Where Propane and Route Density Pay Off

In buildings with 25,000+ sq ft of corridors, lobbies and open-plan hard floors, propane burnishers cut machine time roughly in half. A crew that would need four hours with electric equipment finishes in two, which is why large-floor unit rates fall to $0.012–$0.025. The catch is compliance: propane runs only when the space is unoccupied and ventilated, with carbon monoxide monitoring under OSHA limits. Where landlords ban propane, large buildings stay closer to $0.02–$0.03 with battery ride-on or wide-path electric units.

Large buildings also gain from route density. A vendor with a night crew already on site can schedule burnishing between other tasks, so there is no travel charge or separate minimum. When buyers bid large floors, they should ask for burnishing to be priced as a line inside the nightly contract rather than as a standalone project.
Chemistry Choices That Affect Gloss at Any Size

Chemical residue is the hidden reason some floors refuse to shine. Daily disinfectant mopping with quaternary products can leave film that the burnisher smears. A hydrogen peroxide disinfectant such as the CloroxPro concentrate, with a 30-second to one-minute contact time and no harsh VOC fumes, is commonly used on restroom surfaces and touch points and rinses cleaner, but floors should still be damp mopped with a neutral cleaner before burnishing. In lobbies, ammonia-based glass cleaner like the Zep Commercial Streak-Free formula should be sprayed onto the cloth, not toward the curtain wall, because ammonia overspray softens floor finish along the glass line and shows as dull streaks after the burnish pass.

faqs.q: Why is my small office paying more per square foot than a big building?
faqs.a: Because the vendor's fixed setup time and the $90–$135 per-visit minimum are divided over far fewer square feet. A 1,000 sq ft hard-floor area may only be worth $30–$50 at the unit rate, but the minimum sets the bill. Bundling burnishing into the nightly janitorial visit is the most effective fix.

faqs.q: At what size does a propane burnisher become cost-effective?
faqs.a: Usually above about 15,000 sq ft of contiguous, unoccupied hard floor. Below that, setup time and cylinder handling erase the speed advantage. Propane also requires ventilation and CO monitoring to stay under the OSHA 50 ppm eight-hour limit, so confirm your landlord allows it.

faqs.q: Should burnishing be listed separately in a large-building contract?
faqs.a: List it as its own line with a frequency and unit rate, but inside the base contract. That keeps it auditable for completion and avoids a standalone minimum. Make sure the scope excludes restorative work like scrub-and-recoat, which should be priced separately at $0.18–$0.35 per sq ft.

faqs.q: What documents should I ask for regardless of office size?
faqs.a: A certificate of insurance with general liability and workers compensation, Safety Data Sheets for floor chemicals under OSHA HazCom, and, if you track green purchasing, confirmation that cleaners and finishes meet Green Seal GS-37 or GS-40. Medical suites should also confirm the crew is trained on OSHA bloodborne pathogen procedures for restroom and exam-adjacent floors.

faqs.q: How do I convert per-visit burnishing into a monthly budget?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-visit price by visits per month on a 4.33 weeks-per-month basis: 4.33 for weekly, 2.17 for biweekly and 1 for monthly. A $300 biweekly visit equals about $651 per month.
